about: Matter falling onto anything through a disc (exotic objects design 2.2, package XO2): how fast a body can feed, how much of the mass comes out as light, where the disc ends inside and out, which flow the gas takes, and how much gas a mass sweeps up. One descriptor on any body; it never asks what kind of body it is.

references: Eddington, A. S. 1926, The Internal Constitution of the Stars, Cambridge University Press https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1926ics..book.....E
Frank, J., King, A. and Raine, D. 2002, Accretion Power in Astrophysics, 3rd edn, Cambridge University Press https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2002apa..book.....F
atoms.shown: L_Edd = 4πGM m_p c / σ_T,  Ṁ_Edd = L_Edd / (η c²)

equation.name: How fast a body can feed before its own light pushes the gas away
equation.formula:
Le = 4 * pi * G * M * m_p * c / sigma_T
Me = if eta <= 0 then 0 else Le / (eta * c^2)

M.name: mass of the body being fed

eta.name: share of the infalling mass's rest energy given off as light

source.text: Eddington 1926; Frank, King and Raine 2002, Accretion Power in Astrophysics, section 1.2
source.where: ionised hydrogen, light pushing on free electrons (Thomson scattering), spherical

explain.curious: Light pushes. Gas falling onto anything gets hot and shines, and if it falls too fast its own light blows the rest away. For a body as heavy as the Sun the limit is about 33,000 times the Sun's light.
explain.science: Radiation force on electrons, σ_T L / (4π r² c), balances gravity on the protons they drag, GM m_p / r², at L_Edd = 4πGM m_p c / σ_T ≈ 1.26 × 10³¹ W per solar mass. The rate that gives it is L_Edd / (η c²). Ionised hydrogen; helium-rich gas has a higher limit (fewer electrons per unit mass).

references: Bardeen, J. M., Press, W. H. and Teukolsky, S. A. 1972, Rotating black holes: locally nonrotating frames, energy extraction, and scalar synchrotron radiation, ApJ 178, 347 https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1972ApJ...178..347B

Novikov, I. D. and Thorne, K. S. 1973, Astrophysics of black holes, in Black Holes (Les Astres Occlus), eds. DeWitt, C. and DeWitt, B. S., Gordon and Breach, 343 https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1973blho.conf..343N
Misner, C. W., Thorne, K. S. and Wheeler, J. A. 1973, Gravitation, W. H. Freeman (Schwarzschild geometry, chapters 25 and 31) https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1973grav.book.....M
atoms.shown: η = 1 − (1 − 2r_g/r) / √(1 − 3r_g/r);  inside 6 r_g (a spinning hole's last stable orbit) η = 1 − √(1 − 2r_g/3r)

equation.name: How much of the falling matter's mass comes out as light
equation.formula:
x = r / rg
eta = if x < 6 then 1 - sqrt(max(1 - 2 / (3 * x), 0)) else 1 - (1 - 2 / x) / sqrt(1 - 3 / x)

r.name: where the disc ends on the inside

eta.name: share of rest energy given off as light

source.text: Bardeen, Press and Teukolsky 1972; Novikov and Thorne 1973
source.where: energy of a circular orbit at r, Schwarzschild; at a Kerr last stable orbit E = √(1 − 2/(3x))

explain.curious: Gas spiralling in gives off the energy it loses on the way down. Onto a black hole that is about 6% of its whole mass, many times what burning hydrogen in a star gets (0.7%). Onto a white dwarf it is a few thousandths of a percent.
explain.science: η = 1 − E(r_in), the specific energy of a circular geodesic at the inner edge: E = (1 − 2/x)/√(1 − 3/x) with x = r/r_g (Schwarzschild), 0.0572 at x = 6, → 1/(2x) far out (the Newtonian GM/2r). Inner edges inside 6 r_g are a spinning hole's last stable orbit, where E = √(1 − 2/(3x)) holds for every spin (Bardeen et al. 1972 eq. 2.21): 0.32 at x = 1.24 (a = 0.998). The two agree at x = 6.

params.description: where the field takes over, as a share of the Alfvén radius (Ghosh and Lamb about 0.5; a factor of 2 either way is argued)

references: Ghosh, P. and Lamb, F. K. 1979, Accretion by rotating magnetic neutron stars. III. Accretion torques and period changes in pulsating X-ray sources, ApJ 234, 296 https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1979ApJ...234..296G
Frank, J., King, A. and Raine, D. 2002, Accretion Power in Astrophysics, 3rd edn, Cambridge University Press https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2002apa..book.....F

Bardeen, J. M., Press, W. H. and Teukolsky, S. A. 1972, Rotating black holes: locally nonrotating frames, energy extraction, and scalar synchrotron radiation, ApJ 178, 347 https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1972ApJ...178..347B
atoms.shown: r_in = max(R, r_isco, ξ r_A),  r_A = ((μ₀/4π)² μ⁴ / (2GMṀ²))^(1/7)

equation.name: Where a disc ends on the inside
equation.formula:
ra = if mu <= 0 or Md <= 0 then 0 else ((mu0 / (4 * pi))^2 * mu^4 / (2 * G * M * Md^2)) ^ (1/7)
rm = xi * ra
rin = max(max(R, risco), rm)

M.name: mass of the body being fed

R.name: the body's surface (a black hole's horizon)

mu.name: strength of the body's magnet (dipole moment)

rm.name: where the body's field takes over from the disc

rin.name: where the disc ends on the inside

source.text: Ghosh and Lamb 1979; Frank, King and Raine 2002, section 6.3
source.where: Alfvén radius for spherical infall, disc edge a share ξ of it

explain.curious: A disc stops where something stops it: the body's own surface, the closest a stable orbit can go, or a magnetic field strong enough to grab the gas. That one rule gives a black hole's dark gap, a white dwarf's bright edge and the glowing poles of an X-ray pulsar.
explain.science: The largest of the surface, the last stable orbit and the magnetospheric radius ξ r_A, where magnetic pressure B²/2μ₀ of the dipole matches the ram pressure of the infall: r_A = ((μ₀/4π)² μ⁴ / (2GMṀ²))^(1/7). ξ ≈ 0.5 (Ghosh and Lamb 1979; argued within a factor of 2). A neutron star with μ = 10²⁷ A m² fed 10¹⁴ kg/s holds the disc off at about 1,500 km.

params.description: Paczyński's fitted share of the separation

references: Paczyński, B. 1977, A model of accretion disks in close binaries, ApJ 216, 822 https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1977ApJ...216..822P
Frank, J., King, A. and Raine, D. 2002, Accretion Power in Astrophysics, 3rd edn, Cambridge University Press https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2002apa..book.....F

equation.name: Where the companion's pull cuts a disc off

q.name: the companion's mass over the fed body's

rout.name: where the disc ends on the outside

source.text: Paczyński 1977; Frank, King and Raine 2002, section 5.5
source.where: largest non-crossing orbit in the restricted three-body problem, fitted for 0.03 < q < 1

explain.curious: A disc in a pair of stars cannot grow past where the other star's pull bends its orbits into each other: a little over half the way to the companion.
explain.science: Paczyński (1977) found the largest periodic orbit that does not cross its neighbours; a fit gives r_out ≈ 0.6 a / (1 + q) for 0.03 < q < 1. Tidal truncation, so a fact of the orbit, not of the gas.

params.description: feeding share below which the gas cannot cool and puffs up into a hot thin flow (about α² for viscosity α ≈ 0.1)
feeding share above which the disc swells and blows matter back out
how sharply one flow hands over to the next

references: Narayan, R. and Yi, I. 1994, Advection-dominated accretion: a self-similar solution, ApJ 428, L13 https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1994ApJ...428L..13N
Narayan, R. and Yi, I. 1995, Advection-dominated accretion: underfed black holes and neutron stars, ApJ 452, 710 https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1995ApJ...452..710N
Abramowicz, M. A., Czerny, B., Lasota, J. P. and Szuszkiewicz, E. 1988, Slim accretion disks, ApJ 332, 646 https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1988ApJ...332..646A
Yuan, F. and Narayan, R. 2014, Hot accretion flows around black holes, ARA&A 52, 529 https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ARA%26A..52..529Y

equation.name: Which way matter falls in: hot and puffed up, a thin bright disc, or a thick swollen one
equation.formula:
hot = if s <= 0 then 1 else 1 / (1 + (s / sh)^n)
thick = if s <= 0 then 0 else 1 / (1 + (st / s)^n)
thin = max(1 - hot - thick, 0)
lit = if s <= 0 then 0 else min(s / sh, 1)

s.name: feeding rate as a share of the Eddington rate

sh.name: share below which the flow is hot

st.name: share above which the flow is thick

thin.name: strength of the thin bright disc

hot.name: strength of the hot thin flow

thick.name: strength of the thick swollen disc

lit.name: how well a hot flow shines against a thin disc fed as fast

source.text: Narayan and Yi 1994, 1995; Abramowicz et al. 1988; Yuan and Narayan 2014
source.where: states of accretion by Eddington share; the smooth hand-over between them is argued, not computed

explain.curious: How fast a black hole is fed decides what it looks like. Starved, the gas stays too hot and thin to shine much and you see almost nothing. Fed well, it settles into a thin, blinding disc. Overfed, the disc swells up and blows much of its gas away.
explain.science: Three processes with strengths that blend, not three classes. Below about α² ≈ 0.01 of the Eddington rate the gas cannot cool by radiation and advects its heat inward (ADAF; Narayan and Yi 1994, 1995), radiating a share that falls with the rate (taken ∝ s here, their ε ∝ ṁ scaling). Near and above the Eddington rate the disc thickens and advects or blows out its heat (slim discs; Abramowicz et al. 1988). The joins and the sharpness are argued (Yuan and Narayan 2014 review the states).

params.description: Bondi's number: 1/4 for gas with γ = 5/3, 1.12 for gas held at one temperature

references: Bondi, H. and Hoyle, F. 1944, On the mechanism of accretion by stars, MNRAS 104, 273 https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1944MNRAS.104..273B
Bondi, H. 1952, On spherically symmetrical accretion, MNRAS 112, 195 https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1952MNRAS.112..195B
Frank, J., King, A. and Raine, D. 2002, Accretion Power in Astrophysics, 3rd edn, Cambridge University Press https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2002apa..book.....F

equation.name: How much gas a mass sweeps up from its surroundings
equation.formula:
w = cs^2 + v^2
Md = 4 * pi * lam * G^2 * M^2 * rho / w^(3/2)
racc = 2 * G * M / w

cs.name: sound speed in the surrounding gas

v.name: speed of the mass through the gas

racc.name: distance inside which the gas is captured

source.where: spherical capture (Bondi), with the Bondi-Hoyle interpolation for a moving mass

explain.curious: A heavy thing sitting in thin gas pulls in what comes close enough. The faster it moves or the hotter the gas, the less it catches. This is an upper limit: near real black holes most of that gas is blown out again before it reaches the middle.
explain.science: Bondi (1952) steady spherical accretion, Ṁ = 4πλ G²M²ρ / c_s³ with λ = 1/4 for γ = 5/3, joined to Bondi and Hoyle (1944) for a moving mass by replacing c_s² with c_s² + v². Gas inside r_acc = 2GM/(c_s² + v²) is bound. The Milky Way's centre in hot gas of 130 per cm³ at 1.3 × 10⁷ K captures about 10⁻⁵ solar masses a year; far less reaches the hole (Yuan and Narayan 2014): the block is rough in practice.
